name: Multiple Epiphyseal Dysplasia-Severe Proximal Femoral Dysplasia Syndrome
aliases: Multiple Epiphyseal Dysplasia with Severe Proximal Femoral Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for MED-SPFD Syndrome

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia involving long bones
Severe dysplasia of the proximal femur characterized by coxa vara and irregular femoral head
Early-onset joint stiffness and limited range of motion predominantly affecting hips and knees
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with epiphyseal dysplasia (e.g., COMP, MATN3)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiographic multiple epiphyseal dysplasia plus severe proximal femoral dysplasia with compatible clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; differential diagnosis should exclude other skeletal dysplasias.
